info.description: TXAPI control console and S5 first-batch billing contracts. Management uses session Bearer; model calls use API-key Bearer. Publication revisions are per-process and scoped by epoch. billing.mode=legacy retains availability-first quota behavior, disabled bypasses monetary quota/charging, and strict requires immutable price history, durable balances and a configured per-request user-fee ceiling. Strict reserves the entire ceiling atomically for user and key, settles known final usage once, and retains uncertain/over-ceiling charges for reconciliation. The ceiling bounds collected user charges, not absolute provider spend. Ordinary logs remain droppable and are not the strict ledger. Strict currently supports text chat (explicit single output limit, n=1, no paid tools/media/unknown extensions) and text embeddings only. Administrator-session-only ledger queries and audited resolution of expired pending holds are available. A repeated identical resolution is idempotent; a conflicting one returns 409. Known excess cost requires an explicit cap_usage decision; unknown cost may only be explicitly waived with evidence. Disabled billing permits read-only inspection. Monetary ledger units are decimal strings (1e9 units per currency). Opt-in native foreground Responses supports text/function tools over JSON or SSE through the shared execution chain; strict rejects Responses before reservation. Idempotency-Key is durable and owner/key scoped. Stored foreground responses and Conversations have owner/key-scoped encrypted local history with finite retention, CAS revisions, current authorization and full-context continuation. Private replay remains separate. store=false retains receipt metadata only and cannot use history. Opt-in disabled-billing background tasks support durable native submit/inspect/cancel with temporary encrypted content, including store=false. This is not permanent history or a zero-retention promise. Opt-in native Responses WebSocket uses a single main lane, text/function events and disabled billing. By default store=false or omitted keeps continuation connection-local. Optional responses_ws.persistent_history plus explicit per-round store=true uses shared owner/key-scoped encrypted local history, public local response IDs and complete-context new generations across HTTP/WS or new connections. It requires the Responses runtime; upstream store=false and native-parent removal avoid double context. Unknown executions cannot be resumed or replayed. Hosted tools, media, multiplexing and automatic replay are unsupported. FC-P1-001 adds opt-in disabled-billing single SIWC account/owner/key/model Responses text streaming. Managed bindings use real persisted credentials and CAS revisions. No real-account acceptance is implied. FC-P3-001 adds persisted, version-fenced eligibility feedback and administrator CAS resume for the single managed binding. Unknown resets require manual review; credentials are retained. FC-P7-WS-USAGE-001 adds opt-in disabled native WS-round usage observations to the existing metadata query, with transport and native protocol status distinct from mechanical termination. It does not authorize WS billing. Schema21 requires a matching stopped-write backup for rollback. Native Responses HTTP JSON/SSE, disabled native background and native WS accept named function/custom tools and one-level mixed namespaces. Calls/results and tool_choice preserve namespace separately from name and call_id. Limits are 64 groups, 1..128 unique function/custom members per group, and 1..128 UTF-8 byte group/member/custom names without edge whitespace/control characters. Custom format is optional text or grammar with lark/regex syntax and 1..65536 UTF-8 byte definition; grammar remains opaque and tools execute at the client. Custom input strings and native delta/done events survive JSON/SSE, background replay and encrypted full-context history. Client tool_search is supported only with execution=client, at most one declaration, opaque object parameters/arguments capped at 65536 JSON bytes, and visible ASCII call_id of 1..64 bytes. tool_search_output requires client execution, completed status and 0..128 loaded tools; additional_tools requires developer role. Loaded definitions are restricted to the same bounded function/custom/one-level namespace types, with optional boolean defer_loading on members. Search items survive native events, background replay and encrypted full-context history. Server search, hosted tools, Code Mode/programmatic execution and nested namespaces remain unsupported; cross-protocol Chat and managed-account text-only bindings do not inherit this capability. HTTP missing/null optional namespace/format is unspecified; WS closed fields reject explicit null. Fixed CLI custom conformance uses an explicit local model catalog profile; the client search case uses bundled gpt-5.5 metadata. Complete default model compatibility remains unverified. FC-P4-CODEX-WS-001 adds bounded native client fields: stream=true, include reasoning.encrypted_content, reasoning effort/summary, text verbosity/plain text format, prompt_cache_key and client_metadata; message IDs/status/phase and tool-result IDs survive mapping. generate=false with store=false/omitted uses the same native WS authority and real provider terminal; usage is recorded for each prewarm, never defaulted to zero. Only the latest completed connection-local parent is accepted; unknown prior usage rejects TPM-limited continuation. Opaque reasoning with nonempty encrypted_content and bounded summary/content survives full-context history; bare reasoning references fail. Reasoning events do not fabricate answer progress or completion. Native WS remains disabled-only, one main lane, 256 KiB messages; no automatic provider replay, background/media/hosted tools or persistent prewarm. Pinned Codex 0.163.0 WS conformance independently checks real handshakes, prewarm, tool-result creates, connection reuse and zero HTTP fallback. This is a controlled provider fixture, not real-provider acceptance or complete default-model support.

get.description: Process aggregate admission occupancy is exposed as gateway_admission_requests_active and gateway_admission_attempts_active. gateway_native_ws_enabled distinguishes disabled native WS from an enabled idle runtime. gateway_native_ws_connections_active counts authorized native sessions until Close finishes, not TCP file descriptors or upstream pool connections. gateway_native_ws_rounds_active counts Execute calls including prewarm, authorization/admission and terminal cleanup. Independent request and attempt slots must not be summed as generation count. Native background metrics expose gateway_background_enabled, gateway_background_controls_active (claimed controls through release cleanup, not remote generations or valid leases), gateway_background_snapshot_success and gateway_background_snapshot_timestamp_seconds. The existing retention loop samples only bounded retained metadata with a 500ms context; scraping reads memory. Before the first successful sample, durable counts are omitted. A failed sample retains the last values/time with success=0; consumers must check the timestamp for freshness. gateway_background_jobs uses only fixed stage labels queued/dispatching/remote_active/terminal/uncertain/other and includes tombstones until metadata expiry. gateway_background_replay_pending counts tasks needing event-tail recovery. gateway_background_events_retained and gateway_background_event_bytes describe encrypted event metadata, and gateway_background_reserved_bytes is reserved content capacity, not SQLite/WAL file size. Retained background metadata remains observable when the feature is disabled. These gauges have no identity/model labels, describe approximate owner snapshots and are not execution, recovery, routing or financial authority. A registry without the respective injected snapshot provider omits its group. The existing metrics network access boundary is unchanged.

post.description: Strict billing reserves the configured full user-fee ceiling before execution. Missing/invalid usage or actual cost above this ceiling retains the hold as pending; it never silently treats the call as free or supplements the budget beyond its hold. Unsupported or unpriced billing dimensions return 400 before forwarding. Strict JSON must be UTF-8, contain no repeated object keys and use explicit text message content and typed stream options. The prepared upstream request must preserve the explicit output limit and a single candidate before any durable network attempt starts. max_completion_tokens is supported only on the existing OpenAI-compatible path; cross-protocol conversion is rejected rather than substituted with max_tokens or a default. This check is not a complete input-token or provider-spend bound. Strict execution also requires an exact channel/base URL/protocol/actual-model/operation provider cost contract and independent request budget. The entire conservative attempt bound is durably occupied before sending; failed or unknown attempts do not restore retry capacity. Before every strict attempt, the pinned selling-price and target group-rate snapshot must price the entire contracted input envelope plus the explicit output cap within the durable user-fee reservation. Uncovered or overflowing bounds return 400 billing_fee_limit without starting that attempt; unknown earlier execution remains pending. Before recording an attempt, the final converted JSON body must also satisfy the strict text-only billing allowlist. Unknown fields, tools/media, explicit cache/thinking/non-default service-tier configuration and duplicate keys are rejected with unsupported_billing_dimension. This validation does not prove implicit model behavior or real input-token ceilings. Native OpenAI fields remain on the fast path. Cross-protocol requests reject unrepresentable options with 400 instead of log-only field loss; function tools are currently routed to OpenAI or Anthropic, not Gemini. Strict tools remain unsupported. Strict execution requires a registered input_bound_profile; missing profiles return 503 provider_input_unproven before any upstream I/O or durable attempt, regardless of nonempty operator evidence. Unsupported targets and compatibility proxies cannot inherit an official profile. The final body output limit must exactly match the limit used for cost admission. The openai_chat_v1 profile binds the official gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 endpoint, input ceiling >= 128000, max_completion_tokens <= 16384 and an explicit service_tier=default on the actual request. The gateway never silently substitutes a service tier; this input profile does not certify operator tariffs or rejected-request charging. Strict execution also requires tariff_profile=openai_standard_usd_2026_10_17, currency=USD, rates at or above registered standard floors and explicit credential ID/key SHA-256 bindings. Missing tariff profiles return 503 provider_tariff_unproven; new/rotated credentials or mismatched final authentication headers return 503 provider_credential_unproven. Both refuse before I/O, do not retry or penalize health, and retain holds for earlier unknown execution. A registered standard floor is not certification of credential-specific maximum rates, surcharges, future pricing or rejected-request charging. Optional startup server.forward_upstream_metadata (default false) exposes only a validated final foreground attempt request ID as X-TXAPI-Upstream-Request-ID, plus Retry-After on matching upstream/final 429 or 503. Local metadata takes precedence; other upstream headers are excluded. Background, claimed execution and WS are unchanged. Nonempty model POST bodies are not automatically replayed by the standard HTTP transport via Request.GetBody; any allowed Chat/embeddings retry remains a separate gateway attempt with fresh admission and applicable cumulative cost accounting. Dispatching still does not prove non-execution, and a permitted retry may execute twice at a Provider. Responses remains non-replayable; custom transports must preserve these boundaries.

post.summary: Create a native foreground or opted-in background Response
post.description: Requires responses.enabled and mounted content/credential keys. Limit 1 MiB. Supports text, instructions, native function tools/history and reasoning items; no Chat conversion. Native foreground SSE dispatches only blank-line-delimited LF/CRLF events with a 1 MiB wire-event limit including the delimiter. An unterminated EOF tail is discarded and cannot establish completion. Defaults store=true without injecting that field upstream. Local response IDs are stable across replay; upstream IDs are metadata only. Idempotency-Key (1-256 visible ASCII bytes) is scoped to current owner and API key. Object key order/JSON whitespace do not affect the digest; numeric lexical representations and omitted/defaulted fields remain distinct. A known terminal receipt expires after configured retention (default 24h), allowing reuse; dispatching/unknown receipts do not expire automatically. Stored replay expires earlier (default 1h) or may be unavailable after an output failure; store=false never retains response bodies. A retry in those states returns 409 and never re-executes. Replays reauthorize identity/model and do not create attempts, consume generation RPM or charge again. Stored responses support GET/delete/input_items and local previous_response_id or conversation continuation, mutually exclusive. Expanded stored context is capped at 256 KiB and 1024 items, pinned to the original target and reauthorized per turn; no native parent ID is sent. store=false cannot reference history. background=true additionally requires responses.background.enabled, explicit channel_ids and billing.mode=disabled; legacy/strict reject before acceptance or network I/O. The background input limit is 256 KiB including the private envelope; self-contained text/function tools only, no previous_response_id/conversation. Original stream=true background requests are observed as durable native sequence-numbered SSE and can resume on GET with stream=true and optional starting_after; nil and zero cursors differ. Only original stream=true jobs support event replay. Native task terminal and terminal event persistence are separate facts. Incomplete, unavailable or expired logs never fabricate DONE/completion. A queued local receipt does not prove remote acceptance or completion. Workers persist their target before POST, bind an accepted remote ID, then inspect/cancel/resume only that exact target. Disconnect does not cancel work; unknown dispatch is never blindly resubmitted. Background content (also store=false) has fixed temporary retention (default 10 minutes); idempotency tombstones default to 24h and uncertainty stays protected. Background is not promoted to A02 long-term history. Native WS remains unsupported. Strict returns 400 unsupported_billing_dimension before any monetary reservation. Optional startup server.forward_upstream_metadata (default false) exposes only a validated final foreground attempt request ID as X-TXAPI-Upstream-Request-ID, plus Retry-After on matching upstream/final 429 or 503. Local metadata takes precedence; other upstream headers are excluded. Background, claimed execution and WS are unchanged. Nonempty model POST bodies are not automatically replayed by the standard HTTP transport via Request.GetBody; any allowed Chat/embeddings retry remains a separate gateway attempt with fresh admission and applicable cumulative cost accounting. Dispatching still does not prove non-execution, and a permitted retry may execute twice at a Provider. Responses remains non-replayable; custom transports must preserve these boundaries. Native Responses HTTP JSON/SSE, disabled native background and native WS accept named function/custom tools and one-level mixed namespaces. Calls/results and tool_choice preserve namespace separately from name and call_id. Limits are 64 groups, 1..128 unique function/custom members per group, and 1..128 UTF-8 byte group/member/custom names without edge whitespace/control characters. Custom format is optional text or grammar with lark/regex syntax and 1..65536 UTF-8 byte definition; grammar remains opaque and tools execute at the client. Custom input strings and native delta/done events survive JSON/SSE, background replay and encrypted full-context history. Client tool_search is supported only with execution=client, at most one declaration, opaque object parameters/arguments capped at 65536 JSON bytes, and visible ASCII call_id of 1..64 bytes. tool_search_output requires client execution, completed status and 0..128 loaded tools; additional_tools requires developer role. Loaded definitions are restricted to the same bounded function/custom/one-level namespace types, with optional boolean defer_loading on members. Search items survive native events, background replay and encrypted full-context history. Server search, hosted tools, Code Mode/programmatic execution and nested namespaces remain unsupported; cross-protocol Chat and managed-account text-only bindings do not inherit this capability. HTTP missing/null optional namespace/format is unspecified; WS closed fields reject explicit null. Fixed CLI custom conformance uses an explicit local model catalog profile; the client search case uses bundled gpt-5.5 metadata. Complete default model compatibility remains unverified.

Temporary background SSE uses Cache-Control: no-store.
